title: Integrated Media Planning Lead
description:

W świecie, w którym media są wszędzie i we wszystkim, łączymy najlepsze platformy, ludzi i partnerów, aby tworzyć nieograniczone możliwości wzrostu.  

Dołączając do nas korzystasz z programów przygotowujących do zawodów przyszłości oraz pracujesz ze specjalistami, których kompetencje potwierdzone są certyfikatem DIMAQ . Dzięki naszym autorskim narzędziom, takim jak platforma WPP Open (platforma AI dla marketingu), będziesz pracować na międzynarodowych projektach i wspierać klientów na całym świecie. Więcej informacji możesz znaleźć na stronie wppmedia.com    

 

Gdzie będziesz rozwijać swoje kompetencje?

EssenceMediacom t o marka agencyjna przynależąca do WPP Media. Specjalizujemy się w tworzeniu strategii, które nie tylko optymalizują działania reklamowe, ale także napędzają rozwój biznesu na dużą skalę. Opieramy się na danych i technologii, działamy zarówno dla ludzi, jak i algorytmów, łączymy różnorodne kompetencje, testujemy i uczymy się, a co najważniejsze - ewoluujemy wraz z otoczeniem.

Na co dzień będziesz m.in.:

• planować i prowadzić kampanie 360,

• współpracować przy projektach, które często wykraczają poza typowe media - dużo niestandardów, kreatywnych aktywacji i działań z influencerami,

title: Account Executive, Fed Civilian
description:
ABOUT FACTORY

Our mission is to create a world where software builds and improves itself.

We build the platform for self-improving software development, helping the world's largest enterprise engineering teams turn their organizations into autonomous software factories. Customers including Nvidia, Blackstone, Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), Palo Alto Networks, Adobe, and T-Mobile run Factory to ship code, review PRs, run tests, and deploy continuously - getting smarter with every cycle.

Factory is on the hunt for a Federal Account Executive with deep knowledge of developer tools, AI, and the Federal Civilian market to drive adoption of Factory's agentic engineering platform across U.S. Federal Civilian agencies - turning government engineering organizations into autonomous development systems. You will own a named set of agencies, run strategic multi-stakeholder deals through federal procurement, and help build Factory's federal civilian practice from the field alongside our CEO, VP of Sales, product, and engineering teams.

WHAT YOU WILL DO AND ACHIEVE

- Own a named set of Federal Civilian agency accounts and lead enterprise sales cycles end-to-end: build pipeline, manage evaluations and pilots, navigate procurement, close multi-stakeholder deals through vehicles like GSA Schedule, agency BPAs/IDIQs, and reseller partners.

- Develop the federal channel: cultivate relationships with prime systems integrators and delivery partners so they embed Factory into their own contract vehicles, solutions, and service offerings.

- Educate and guide agencies through the technical and practical adoption of AI-driven development tools - addressing risk, security, and compliance concerns while showcasing measurable engineering outcomes and ROI.

- Establish Factory as a trusted partner for federal customers, driving expansion and renewals by aligning to their long-term modernization roadmaps, and feed market intelligence back to product and marketing.

QUALIFICATIONS

- 7+ years of sales experience, including 4+ years selling technology into the U.S. Federal Civilian agencies (e.g., VA, USDA, Dept of Energy, Treasury, Commerce, DHS, or independent agencies), managing complex sales cycles from start to finish.

- Proven track record of achieving and exceeding sales targets, with hands-on experience navigating federal procurement (GSA Schedule, BPAs, IDIQs) and selling through or alongside systems integrators and resellers.

- Strategic selling expertise: multi-threading executive relationships, building multi-year account plans, and navigating long budget and procurement cycles tied to the federal fiscal year.

- Exceptional technical aptitude across infras

title: AI-First Product Manager (Ops Transformation)
description:
About Kompato AI
We’re transforming the debt collection industry with AI-powered automation that delivers compliant, empathetic, and revenue-driving customer experiences. Our mission is to help agencies, lenders, and financial institutions reimagine collections by blending human-level conversation with the efficiency of AI. We’re a fast-growing fintech startup building the operating backbone for modern collections-whether inbound, outbound, or digital self-service.
If you’re energized by stripping down messy, manual processes and rebuilding them as AI-native workflows, and if you can translate operational pain into automation that sticks, this role might be for you.
How you will make an impact in this role
We are looking for our first AI-First Product Manager (Ops Transformation) - a builder who fuses product management rigor with systems-level AI thinking.
Your mandate: take our debt collection operator’s playbook, strip it to the studs, and redesign it for an AI-native organization. That means immersing yourself in daily ops, identifying compliance-heavy bottlenecks, and rethinking how they should work in an AI-first world. You’ll own the journey from raw operator pain → prototype automation → adoption and scaling.
This is a role for someone equally comfortable shadowing frontline staff, drafting RICE + risk-scored automation priorities, and guiding MVP engineering builds (or prototyping in Cursor/Claude code yourself). In short: you’ll turn ambiguity into working automations and repeatable playbooks that compound value across departments.
Responsibilities
Discovery & Translation

• Immerse in daily collections ops to map SOPs and surface pain points.

• Apply Jobs-to-Be-Done and anthropological methods to reframe operator needs.

• Identify and rank-order automation opportunities by reach, impact, compliance risk, and more (RICE + risk-tier).

Design & Execution

• Draft specs and either prototype yourself or manage lightweight engineering builds.

• Ship scrappy MVPs quickly; measure cycle-time, compliance adherence, and throughput.

• Capture learnings in shareable posts, SOPs, and the AI-First Ops Handbook so wins compound.

Governance & Compliance

• Apply strict guardrails: T0-T3 risk tiers, human-in-the-loop where required.

• Define automation governance artifacts (SLAs, SOPs, audit logs).

• Ensure AI workflows are explainable, auditable, and compliant.

Impact & Scaling

• Track adoption: % of ops tasks starting with AI.

• Measure business outcomes: revenue impact, FTE leverage, error reduction.

• Industrialize successful prototypes into repeatable modules.

Requirements
Must have

• 5+ years in product management, ops transformation, or program management.

• Proven track record of translating manual SOPs into automated, governed workflows.

• Experience working in or adjacent to regulated industries (fintech, healthcare, collections, gov).

• Familiarity with automation stacks (RPA, workflow orchestration, APIs) and emerging AI architectures (LLMs, agentic systems).

• Data self-service skills (SQL, dashboards) a plus.

• Startup-tested: you can bring order without needing layers of process to get going.

Preferred

• Start with AI: treat automation as the reflexive first step in ops design.

• Human as router: know when to elevate to judgment, compliance, or context.

title: Independent Consultancy - Technical Planning and Coordination
description:
Terms of Reference: Independent Consultancy - Technical Planning and Coordination for the Open Energy Research and Analytics Consortium (ORA)
Background:The Open Energy Research and Analytics Consortium (ORA) is an open energy data partnership between the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), Ember, Global Energy Monitor (GEM), Open Energy Transition (OET), and TransitionZero. Through a shared governance structure and a Secretariat currently housed at GEM, the consortium is working to build an open energy intelligence system based on trusted data, open-source tools, and collaborative analysis.
ORA’s members have already developed the expertise to build every component needed for a shared open data infrastructure as well as reproducible modeling, data pipelines, versioned and citable data, quality metadata, exploration tools, and aggregate data for validation. These components have not yet been coordinated in a cohesive system, and many of the ORA organizations have built similar supporting infrastructure separately. This leaves users and partners to repeatedly reconcile definitions, identifiers, formats, and methodologies, which limits interoperability, auditability, and reuse. The growing use of AI systems for energy questions adds urgency: the standardization, versioning, and source documentation needed to integrate data across ORA are also needed to make open, verified, citable data legible to AI systems.
ORA is entering a 12-month foundational phase to turn the consortium’s vision into an agreed technical and governance blueprint for an open energy data platform and orchestration system, including its audiences, governance, shared standards, and technical architecture for integrating member datasets, open models, and analyses. ORA is committed to ensuring that its core datasets, shared infrastructure, and collaborative tools remain open-source and publicly available.
Objective: ORA seeks an independent consultant, serving as Technical Coordinator, to facilitate and project manage the technical planning of building a shared data infrastructure across the five member organizations. The consultancy includes the interviews and research needed to develop concrete, detailed proposals for how members’ data can be integrated and supports members in agreeing on shared standards, a recommended architecture, and a roadmap for the next phase of the platform and the flagship product, the Open Energy Outlook. The result will be a consortium plan co-authored with the members.
Scope of Work: The Consultant will provide facilitation, project management, and technical analysis for ORA’s defined 12-month foundational planning phase. The Consultant will carry out the following work:

• Facilitation and Consortium Engagement:

• Facilitate the planning process with all five ORA members, preparing agendas and materials, guiding discussions, building consensus among members with different practices and priorities, and documenting decisions and next steps.

• Interview the data leads at each member organization to assess data assets, systems, workflows, and priority user needs.

• Facilitate a shared definition of the platform’s priority users (for example, energy modelers, policy analysts, journalists, civil-society researchers, planners in developing geographies, and AI systems) and the access patterns, tools, and guarantees each needs.

• Lead members through review of, and decisions on, the proposed shared protocols, architecture options, and data hub scope, ensuring all members have meaningful input.

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
We are an AI-first company building innovative agentic frameworks, the systems that let LLM-driven agents research, plan, and act reliably in production. That means orchestrating multi-step workflows with retries, skips, and parallel execution; keeping long-running work persistent and observable; and serving per-tenant retrieval at scale. This isn't about wrapping an LLM in an API call, it's the hard backend engineering that makes agents dependable.
Our stack is Python ( FastAPI ) on AWS , with Terraform. We hire on engineering depth and judgment, not on a keyword count, and we work in whichever language you're strongest in during the interview (more below). As a Senior Engineer, you will own backend services and the orchestration layer on top of them, from design through deployment, operation, and the on-call that follows.
Our team is based in Tehran and pays salaries monthly in USD .
What You Will Do:

• Design, build, and own backend services and the agent-orchestration layer end to end.

• Build resilient systems that stay correct under load and degrade gracefully when a model, tool, or dependency fails.

• Ensure operational excellence by making long-running, multi-step work observable and debuggable in production.

• Shape technical direction through rigorous code reviews, mentorship, and pushing back on specifications when they misalign with engineering reality.

• Drive the full software development lifecycle , translating ambiguous requirements into durable architectures and actionable technical plans.

What We Are Looking For:

• 5+ years building and operating production backend systems , with deep ownership of at least one non-trivial service you can talk through end to end.

• Deep fluency in your primary backend language , and the ability to pick up a new one fast. We work in Python ; if it is not your daily language today, we expect you to ramp quickly.

• Strong systems fundamentals - concurrency, data modeling, and failure modes - and the judgment to choose the right abstraction rather than the cleverest one.

• Sound reasoning under ambiguity : you ask the clarifying question first, make the trade-offs explicit, and adapt when the constraints change.

• Solid grasp of infrastructure and operations , including message brokers (Kafka, RabbitMQ), SQL and NoSQL stores, and running services in containers with an orchestrator (Kubernetes, ECS, Nomad, or similar).

• Professional written English , enabling you to write crisp design documents and align stakeholders on complex technical trade-offs.

Even Better:

• AWS (especially ECS) and Terraform, or comparable cloud and Infrastructure-as-Code experience.

• Hands-on work with LLM, agentic, or RAG systems (LangChain, CrewAI, OpenAI/Anthropic SDKs, Hugging Face) and a real grasp of how non-deterministic agent steps differ from ordinary functions.

• A recognized-bar engineering background, owned open-source work, or another verifiable standout signal.

How We Hire:
We use a deliberate, transparent two-stage process designed to see how you think and build:

• 1. A 120-minute conversation focusing on your background and a collaborative system-design exercise and cultural fit..

• 2. A 120-minute live technical session involving code review, live coding, and a self-review.

You may complete the technical session in your strongest language (Python, Go, Java, Kotlin, PHP, or TypeScript/Node.js). Web search is encouraged; AI assistants are not used. We want to see your fundamental engineering judgment.
What We Offer:

• Competitive USD-based salary and a comprehensive benefits package.

• Hybrid work flexibility with hours that support deep work.

• The opportunity to work at the frontier of agentic AI , tackling hard problems with high ownership.

• A highly educated, agile senior team that values pragmatism, learning, and continuous improvement.

If you would rather be judged on how you think than on a buzzword list, we would like to talk!

We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.
Who We Are
Every Netflix membership, from the moment someone signs up to every plan change, renewal, and cancellation flows through our platform. The Membership & Monetization Platform (MMP) team owns the commerce backbone of Netflix : the Tier 0 services that manage subscription state, pricing, and plan availability for ~330 million members across 190+ countries, handling millions of requests per second.

• You have a platform mindset: You can take vague business directives and translate them into scalable and maintainable solutions.

The Power Marketing Analyst will support the analysis of power market trends, risk assessment, regulatory developments, and other insights that inform the company's power marketing and origination strategy for its solar and energy storage project development portfolio. title: Director of Infrastructure
description:
Expo is agentic mobile infrastructure for building, shipping, and running native apps for iOS, Android, and the web. Millions of developers and AI agents use Expo's open-source framework and cloud services to go from idea to production, with tools to build, submit to the app stores, ship over-the-air updates, and monitor performance and crashes at scale. Founded in 2015, Expo is on a mission to make great software development accessible to everyone.

About the Role

We're looking for a hands-on Director of Infrastructure to lead and scale the infrastructure systems that power our engineering and product organizations. This is a high-impact leadership role responsible for the reliability, scalability, performance, and evolution of our core infrastructure across platform engineering, data pipelines, billing systems, fleet management, and multi-cloud environments.

The ideal candidate combines deep technical expertise with strong leadership, strategic vision, and excellent communication skills. They run real work through agents (swarms, automation, loops) and lead their teams to do the same by owning the trust model for what agents can perform independently, what requires human guidance, and what guardrails apply.

This is not a purely managerial role: we need a leader who can set direction while remaining close to the technology, troubleshoot complex problems, participate in on-call rotations, and execute directly alongside the team.

We're particularly interested in candidates who have built and scaled infrastructure in a small, fast-moving company and who are comfortable balancing hands-on execution with technical leadership and team development.

What You'll Do

•
Define infrastructure strategy: Define infrastructure strategy and execution through the roadmap and standards, ensuring everything we run is reliable and scalable. Set priorities and weigh long-term work against operational needs, so systems scale with the needs of engineering and product.

•
Own platform infrastructure: Own macOS and Linux fleets, developer infrastructure, code review systems and provisioning, ensuring they are secure, reliable and cost-effective. Build automation and configuration management, run observability, and manage lifecycle management across every system, so these are platforms that engineers can rely on.

•
Run data and billing infrastructure: Run data pipelines and data engineering systems, ensuring reliability, scalability, correctness and operational resilience. Build and operate billing infrastructure, so business-critical workflows keep running.

•
Scale fleet management: Scale macOS and Linux fleet management, ensuring elastic capacity, efficient resource use and reliable operations. Plan and lead multi-cloud expansion, so infrastructure keeps up as demands grow.

•
Lead operational reliability: Lead reliability, performance and availability, and join on-call rotations alongside the team. Run incident response, troubleshoot complex issues and take direct ownership of critical problems, so production stays up.

•
Contribute hands-on technical depth: Contribute to architecture, implementation and debugging alongside the team. Drive operational improvements and mentor engineers, so the technical bar rises across the team.

•
Partner with engineering and product: Partner with engineering and product to communicate strategy, trade-offs, risks and progress, ensuring the message is clear. Shape infrastructure investments so they support the organization's goals and let teams move quickly.

•
Deliver elastic compute at scale: You make sure Expo always has the compute customers need across multiple clouds and regions, so builds, CI, and Simulators scale with demand. You keep cost per minute falling as volume grows, plan capacity ahead of launches and peak usage, and, starting next year, work with me (Joe) to find, evaluate, and build or acquire data center warehouses for our Mac and Linux fleet.

title: Complaints Reviewer
description:
Job title: Complaints Reviewer x2
Apply Before: 13/11/2026, 23:55
Locations: Remote (UK Wide)
Starting Salary (£) 44,139
Working Hours : 35
Contract Type: Permanent
Headline
Manage and review enquiries and complaints for the final ombudsman-style stage of a new standardised process for complaints about how safeguarding concerns have been handled by Church of England bodies. Handle enquiries and complaints in a fair, independent and timely manner, helping to deliver a high-quality complaints handling service and improve organisational learning.
Description
The Church of England’s Safeguarding Structures Reform Programme is delivering a programme to strengthen safeguarding and rebuild trust. The Programme will roll out a standardised process across Church of England bodies for complaints about how safeguarding matters have been handled. Where matters cannot be resolved locally, they can be referred to an independent complaints body to review and make a final determination.
The Complaints Reviewer is responsible for reviewing complaints and enquiries, carrying out investigations, gathering and assessing evidence, and making recommendations to the Independent Complaints Adjudicator. The role supports effective, transparent and empathetic complaint handling while contributing to service improvement and stakeholder confidence.
The postholder will work closely with the Independent Complaints Adjudicator, colleagues and external stakeholders, balancing casework delivery with continuous improvement and the promotion of best practice in complaints handling. The Complaints Reviewer may be delegated additional responsibilities by the Independent Complaints Adjudicator as relevant.
Responsibilities
Key responsibilities will include:

description:
The Opportunity
AI is changing the economics of legal practice. Work that once took hours can increasingly be done in minutes, creating both enormous leverage for lawyers and new pressure to win and serve more clients efficiently.
Yet solo practitioners and small law firms still face many of the same constraints: missed calls, slow follow-up, intake handled between client matters, inconsistent marketing, and administrative work competing with billable time. Building larger intake, administrative, and marketing teams is expensive and increasingly unnecessary.
BloomLex is building a different model: a managed AI workforce that helps small law firms grow without growing their team.
The customer thesis has been validated through live pilots, and multiple deployments are moving into production evaluation. The next phase is proving in-production reliability, delivery economics, repeatability, and scalability. The companies that successfully deploy trusted AI workers into professional-service verticals over the next 18 months have an opportunity to define entirely new categories. We intend to be one of them.
The Venture
BloomLex is building an AI workforce for solo practitioners and small law firms, helping them win and serve more clients without adding headcount.
We call the broader shift the Rise of the Solo: AI gives an individual lawyer or a small firm access to capabilities that historically required a much larger organization.
Unlike self-serve software, BloomLex is fully managed. We configure, deploy, monitor, and continuously improve the AI workforce for each firm. Our customers evaluate us on outcomes - calls answered, prospective clients captured, consultations booked, demand generated, follow-up completed, and time saved - not on how much software they configure themselves.
Our Bloomlex workforce starts with two teammates:
Ava - AI Front Desk. Ava answers calls 24/7, handles structured intake, screens and routes inquiries, books consultations, performs outbound callbacks and follow-up, and integrates those interactions into the firm's workflow.
Claire - AI Marketing Assistant. Claire helps firms generate and nurture demand through content, digital marketing, campaign management and optimization, lead nurturing, and ongoing marketing execution.
Together, Ava and Claire address both sides of growth: Claire helps create demand; Ava helps ensure that demand is captured and converted.
They are also the beginning, not the end, of the platform. Our roadmap expands the AI workforce across the operational side of the practice - including custom workflows and additional specialized AI roles - all delivered through the same managed model and coordinated around the lawyer.
The Partnership
The CEO co-founder is in place. The customer thesis is validated, design partners are engaged, live pilots are running, and the initial product architecture exists. What remains is to bring on the technical co-founder - a partner who will own product and engineering with the same conviction, urgency, and ownership as the CEO.
This is a co-founder role, not a CTO hire. In return for that level of commitment, you receive founder-level equity, founder-level authority with decision collaboration on product, technology, hiring, fundraising, and strategy, and a genuine partnership with the CEO on every material decision.
You will inherit working products and live deployments, but you will not inherit sacred architecture. Your job is to determine what should survive, what should be rebuilt, and what needs to exist for BloomLex to scale from pilots to thousands of firms.
Role & Responsibilities
As Co-Founder & CTO, you will be a hands-on builder first and the architect of the technical organization that follows.

title: Rust Senior Software Engineer – Bare Metal as a Service & Datacenter Networking
description:
About the Team
Our engineering team builds next-generation, cloud-native bare-metal orchestration platforms for AI neo-cloud environments. We operate on a T-shaped engineering model: while each engineer brings deep expertise in a primary domain, every team member maintains practical fluency across neighboring systems. This shared foundation enables rigorous design reviews, effective cross-domain code reviews, and dependable on-call coverage. Our development is fundamentally based on open-source projects, and contributing to them is a major part of our work.
We develop primary control plane software in Rust and Go, leverage Kubernetes operators, and foster an OpenTelemetry-first operational culture.
Role Overview
We are seeking a Senior Software Engineer who combines strong software architecture principles with deep technical domain expertise in Datacenter Networking and DPU architectures. Fitting into our T-shaped engineering model, you will drive the development of control planes powering high-density, high-throughput infrastructure for AI training and inference workloads. Familiarity with automated bare-metal provisioning and lifecycle management is a strong asset.
Core Responsibilities

• Control Plane Development: Design, build, and maintain production-grade control plane microservices, custom Kubernetes operators, and robust reconciliation engines in Rust and Go.

• Architecture & API Design: Author clear Functional (FR) and Non-Functional Requirements (NFR), architectural specs, system sequence diagrams, and clean gRPC/Protobuf and REST API schemas.

• Network Integration: Develop custom integration modules and integrations for modern network operating systems (SONiC, NVUE, Cumulus) and DPU hardware platforms.

• Observability & Diagnostics: Instrument services end-to-end using OpenTelemetry (OTel) traces and metrics, performing systematic root-cause analysis across polyglot distributed systems.

• Quality & Engineering Excellence: Participate in rigorous, review-gated pull request workflows across Rust, Go, and SQL codebases while ensuring high test coverage via mock-driven testing.

• Language Proficiency: Primary mastery of Rust (Tokio async runtime, Tonic, Axum, sqlx) and strong proficiency in Go.

• Data & APIs: Advanced SQL / PostgreSQL fluency, gRPC/Protobuf contract design, and schema evolution.

• Concurrency & Reliability: Strong background in async concurrency models, lock-free patterns, distributed state handling, and mock-driven testing discipline.

• Datacenter Protocols & OS: Expertise in BGP, MP-BGP, EVPN, VXLAN, L3VNI, route targets, and route server design. Hands-on experience with SONiC, Cumulus Linux, and NVUE (featuring a first-class NVUE client).

• DPU & Fabric Ecosystem: Deep knowledge of NVIDIA DOCA, Host-Based Networking (HBN), BlueField DPU architectures, and the DPF (DOCA Platform Framework) operator model (BFB, DPUSet, DPUNode CRDs).

• High-Performance Interconnects: Understanding of InfiniBand fabrics, NVLink / NMX-M partitioning, and RoCEv2.

• Linux Kernel Networking: Advanced grasp of Linux netlink, network namespaces, routing tables, and internal DHCP/DNS service implementations (the project ships its own services).

• Cloud & Kubernetes Networking: Familiarity with CNI plugins (Calico, Cilium). OVS and DPDK experience is a plus.

• Provisioning & Boot Infrastructure: Expertise in PXE/iPXE, UEFI, Secure Boot, measured boot, and TPM attestation.

• Hardware Management: Proficiency in Redfish, IPMI, and BMC abstractions across heterogeneous hardware platforms (Dell, Lenovo, NVIDIA reference hardware).

• Linux Systems Internals: In-depth knowledge of boot chains, systemd, initramfs, BIOS configuration matrices.

• Identity & Security: Practical experience with PKI, X.509 certificates, TLS, SPIFFE/SVID, Vault, KMS, Keycloak (OAuth2/JWT), and RBAC.

• Virtualization: Experience with KubeVirt / KVM.

title: Senior Kreditorenbuchhalter (m/f/d)
description:
Bei Statista dreht sich alles um Daten und Fakten, denn wir sind die weltweit führende Business Data Plattform. Durch die Bereitstellung verlässlicher und einfach nutzbarer Daten sowie verschiedener Datenanalyseprodukte und -dienstleistungen unterstützen wir Menschen weltweit, faktenbasierte Entscheidungen zu treffen.

2007 in Hamburg gegründet, haben wir uns schnell zu einem globalen Unternehmen mit Büros in Metropolen wie London, New York und Tokio entwickelt. Und wir haben auch weiterhin viel vor. Unser stetiges Wachstum ist nicht nur Beweis für unseren Erfolg, sondern schafft auch immer neue Entwicklungs- und Karrieremöglichkeiten für unsere Mitarbeiter:innen.

Wir schätzen und feiern unsere vielfältige Kultur. Hier bist Du willkommen, egal, wer Du bist, woher Du kommst, wie Du aussiehst oder welche Graphen und Diagramme Du bevorzugst. Deine Geschichte ist wichtig - schreibe sie weiterhin als Teil unseres Teams. Überzeuge dich selbst und werde Teil unseres Teams!

Dein Job

'• Kreditorenbuchhaltung im Tagesgeschäft: Du bearbeitest Eingangsrechnungen und klärst Abweichungen und offene Posten eigenständig. Auch bei hohem Volumen sorgst du für zügige Bearbeitung und verlässlich hohe Qualität.

• Verantwortung für den Prozess: Du behältst den gesamten Purchase-to-Pay-Prozess (P2P) im Blick - von Bestellung über Wareneingang und Rechnungsprüfung bis zur Zahlung - und arbeitest eng mit den beteiligten Teams zusammen.

• Abschlüsse und Abstimmungen: Du stimmst Kreditorenkonten ab, bearbeitest Klärfälle und lieferst belastbare Beiträge zu den Monats-, Quartals- und Jahresabschlüssen.

• Prozessverbesserung und Projekte: Du analysierst bestehende Abläufe über Teamgrenzen hinweg, identifizierst Engpässe und setzt Verbesserungen gemeinsam mit den relevanten Schnittstellen um.

• Automatisierung und KI: Du prüfst, wo Automatisierung und KI die Bearbeitung sinnvoll unterstützen können, und gestaltest Lösungen mit, die Effizienz und Qualität verbessern - mit angemessenen Kontrollen und fachlicher Prüfung.

Dein Profil

'• Fundierte Praxis in der Kreditorenbuchhaltung: Du beherrschst das operative Geschäft sicher, priorisierst auch bei hohem Belegaufkommen gut und lieferst eigenständig präzise Ergebnisse.

• End-to-End-Verständnis: Du kennst die wesentlichen Teilbereiche des P2P-Prozesses aus der Praxis und hast bereits Projekte zur Analyse oder Verbesserung bereichsübergreifender Abläufe begleitet.

• SAP-Erfahrung: Du hast in der Kreditorenbuchhaltung mit SAP gearbeitet; Erfahrung mit SAP S/4HANA ist besonders willkommen.

• Gestaltungswille: Du hinterfragst Routinen konstruktiv, denkst über die eigene Aufgabe hinaus und setzt Verbesserungen pragmatisch um.

• Offenheit für neue Technologien: Du interessierst dich dafür, wie Automatisierung und KI Kreditorenprozesse verbessern können. Spezifische KI-Toolkenntnisse setzen wir nicht voraus.

• Sprachen: Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift.

Was wir bieten

Neben unserem großartigen Team, unserer Unternehmenskultur und dem gemeinsamen Ziel, Menschen mit Daten zu empowern, gibt es viele weitere Gründe, warum Statista ein großartiger Arbeitsplatz ist! Werde Teil unseres Teams und profitiere von folgenden Vorteilen:

- Arbeiten aus dem Ausland: 10 Tage pro Jahr (bis zu 30 Tage, wenn deine Familie im Ausland lebt)

- Hybrides Arbeiten und flexible Arbeitszeiten

- Internationales Team und regelmäßige Teamevents

title: Lifecycle Growth Manager
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.

SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.

LIFECYCLE GROWTH MANAGER

Lifecycle Growth's job is to get more people using Grok, Grok Bot, X, SpaceXSI and the API every day, and to turn that use into revenue. We own everything after signup: getting people to value, converting them to paid, growing their teams and keeping them coming back. We do it with lifecycle marketing, in-product messaging and a steady stream of experiments, and much of the work runs on agents we build ourselves.

This isn't a traditional marketing role. You'll do the work of a product manager, a product marketer and a marketing engineer, often in the same day. You'll own lifecycle growth for one or more of our products. You'll figure out where the biggest opportunity is, design the program, build it and show whether it actually moved the number.

The job spans consumer and business, self-serve and sales-led, so you'll need to think as clearly about a solo user's first week as about a team's path to an enterprise deal. You'll go deep on the systems underneath, like who's eligible, what triggers a message, how events and attributes are modeled, and how data moves from the warehouse into our messaging tools. When the best fix lives in the product or the data, you'll make the case and either build it yourself or work with engineering to ship it.

- Strategy and roadmap: Own lifecycle end to end across our suite of products: Grok, Grok Build, Grok Bot, X and the API, from activation and conversion to paid through team expansion, retention and winback.

- Data and audiences: Use SQL and product data to size opportunities, build the audiences and triggers behind each program, and prove what actually drove revenue.

- Journeys: Architect multi-step, cross-channel programs across email, push and in-app, with event-based triggers, branching and suppression logic, and personalization drawn from product usage, plan and billing state, and company and role enrichment.

- Systems: Drive and continuously improve the data model lifecycle runs on, including identity, events, attributes and eligibility, and partner with engineering on the warehouse syncs, APIs and webhooks that keep it accurate in real time.

- Measurement: Run every program as an experiment with a proper holdout, measure incremental lift, and make judgment calls when a result is inconclusive.

- Portfolio: Manage lifecycle as a portfolio of programs, putting more behind what works and retiring what doesn't.

- In-product: Own in-product messaging and experiments, from onboarding and upgrade prompts to post-purchase plan tours, and partner with product and engineering to improve our in-app comms systems.

- Tooling: Use code and agents to build the internal tools, templates and automated QA the team runs on, so each new program ships faster than the last.

- 8+ years in Lifecycle, Growth PMM or Product Growth at a high-growth product company.

- Hands-on experience running lifecycle programs in a major lifecycle platform, such as Braze, Customer.io or Iterable.

title: Data Center Capacity Engineer II
description:
As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed - we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

About the Role:
Support Data Center capacity planning across CrowdStrike's global data center footprint. You'll assign and track power, space, cooling, rack, and fiber port capacity; maintain forecasting models and dashboards; and partner with Data Center Operations, Network Engineering, Supply Chain, and Systems Infrastructure teams to ensure capacity is available ahead of demand.

What You'll Do:

• Assign power, space, and rack capacity to incoming deployment requests; maintain allocation and reservation records

• Maintain and update capacity models for power, space, cooling, cabinet, and structured cabling/port availability across all sites

• Track fiber port capacity, utilization, and projected consumption across MDF and IDF locations - available vs. in-use patch panel ports, by site, by room, and by panel

• Track vendor and carrier cross-connect port usage across PoP and DC facilities, including quantity in service, media/connector type, and growth against contracted or available positions

• Submit expansion demand to DC Build ahead of fiber port or cross-connect exhaustion

• Produce recurring capacity reporting and dashboards; surface constraint and threshold-breach risks to the DC Management

• Translate server/storage/network demand forecasts into rack-level deployment plans and site allocation recommendations

• Partner with Deployment Engineering and DC Ops on rack elevations, placement, and burn-down of installed vs. reserved capacity

• Maintain data accuracy in DCIM/asset systems; drive reconciliation between DCIM, AssetDB, and physical audits

• Support colo expansion and site build inputs: requirements gathering, capacity validation, and tracking of contracted vs. consumed power

• Contribute to automation of reporting and data collection.

• Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

What You'll Need:

• US Citizen or Green Card Holder

• 2-5 years in data center capacity planning, DC operations, infrastructure engineering, or related

• Working knowledge of DC power distribution (UPS, RPP PDU, branch circuits, A/B feeds, redundancy models N+1/2N), cooling, and rack/space planning

• Strong Excel/Google Sheets modeling

• Experience with a DCIM platform (Nlyte, Sunbird, Device42, or similar) and BI tooling (Tableau, Power BI, Grafana)

• Ability to interpret rack elevations, one-lines, and floor plans

Bonus Points:

• Hyperscale or large colo environment experience; multi-region footprint

• Familiarity with network capacity concepts (port/fabric/uplink utilization)

• Experience tracking cross-connect inventory in a DCIM or IPAM

title: AI Enablement Lead
description:
PLEASE NOTE: This role is 5 days/week on-site in our NYC (Manhattan) office

ABOUT US

Legora is redefining how legal work gets done. Not built for lawyers, built with them. We work alongside the world’s best legal teams, who expect excellence, precision, and speed, and we hold ourselves to the same bar.

Our AI-native workspace lets legal professionals move faster, think more clearly, and operate with sharper precision. By analysing thousands of documents in minutes and powering end-to-end workflows, we cut through complexity, teams can focus on what matters: judgment, strategy, and outcomes.

2,100+ customers across 80+ countries trust us, including Cleary Gottlieb, Goodwin, Linklaters, White & Case, Dentons, and Barclays. We’ve scaled to $200M+ in ARR, with teams across Europe, North America and APAC, and continue to expand through acquisitions including Qura, Walter AI, Graceview, Cadastral, and Wexler.

We partner with world-class performers: including Aaron Judge and the New York Yankees, Ludvig Åberg (and his caddie), and campaigns featuring Jude Law.

Joining Legora means three things.

- We lean in: ownership over titles, outcomes over intentions.

- We fight for excellence: high standards, direct, ego-free feedback.

- We grow together: as a team and with our customers.

Mission before ego. Everyone contributes. No one coasts.

If you’re driven by impact, pace, and raising the bar. This is the place.

The Role

AI is reshaping how legal work gets done, and at Legora we're not just watching that happen. We're building it from the inside.

Our AI Enablement function exists to make sure every team at Legora can build, use, and govern AI well. The function is young, the mandate is broad, and right now it's one person. You'd be joining to own a significant slice of that work: managing engineers, translating business needs into action, and becoming the go-to for anything AI across the organization.

This is a high-ownership generalist seat for someone energized by ambiguity who would rather figure it out and ship than wait for a perfect brief.

 

What You'll Be Doing

We operate across three streams, and you'll own initiatives in all of them, from rough idea to shipped result.

Build

- Coordinate agent and internal tool builds with engineers, keeping projects moving and translating between business needs and technical direction.

Enable

- Run training, workshops, and documentation that help teams adopt AI.

- Build and grow an AI champions program across the org.

- Be the day-to-day support that makes enablement actually land.

Govern

- Draft and operationalize guidelines, access policies, and usage guardrails.

- Put the standards in place that let us move fast safely.

Across all three, you'll act as a connector, building the relationships and touchpoints that make the function visible and trusted.

 

Who You Are

- A few years in a fast-moving environment: ops, strategy, product, consulting, program management, or similar. Shape matters more than title.

- Genuinely AI-native, or clearly on the way: you reach for AI tools by default and want to go deeper.

- True generalist: comfortable switching between strategy, delivery, and people work in the same day.

- Exceptional learning speed: you get to depth on unfamiliar things fast and take feedback in quickly.

- Strong communicator with a low-ego, collaborative style.

- Someone who enjoys being in the office 5 days a week. A key component of Legora's success has been in-person collaboration and we want you to be part of that.

 

Nice To Have

- Technical foundation: engineering degree (or equivalent), with enough coding exposure to hold your own with engineers.

- Exposure to legal, GTM, or a regulated / high-trust environment.

- Experience with agent platforms, workflow tools, or no/low-code AI.

- A track record of starting something from scratch.

 

What Success Looks Like (The First 6 Months)

- You're independently owning initiatives end-to-end across all

We are seeking a highly skilled Servicenow CSM Developer to join our IT Services team. title: Customer Success Manager
description:
Workiva Customer Success Managers (CSM) are a critical part of our customer-facing team. CSMs serve as the primary point of contact for customers, managing the entire customer lifecycle by focusing on business outcomes; and identifying opportunities for growth within their named accounts post-sale. As a CSM, your primary mission will be to maximize our customers return on investment (ROI) in the Workiva Platform. You will develop and maintain close relationships with management, product adoption sponsors, and/or key stakeholders throughout the customer lifecycle. You will work closely with Workiva ’s Services team, Support team, Marketing team, and Sales team to drive adoption by ensuring customers are effectively onboarded, trained, and supported throughout the customer journey.
What You’ll Do

• Drive customer adoption of Workiva solutions

• Ensure continuous ROI to your customers

• Consult on best practices, workflows, and management business reviews

• Develop multi-purpose relationships throughout customer organizations

• Identify risks within named accounts & take appropriate actions to manage and/or escalate to an efficient resolution

• Ensure all customers are continuously working toward key milestones of the Customer Journey using customer-facing Success Plans

• Advocate for customers internally by providing continuous feedback to Workiva ’s Sales, Services, Marketing, Product, & Engineering teams

• Work with Sales to understand the details of upcoming renewals

• Teach customers how to use the Workiva Platform

• Use customer management tools to track customer communication, issues, and metrics

What You'll Need
Minimum Qualifications

• Undergraduate degree or equivalent combination of experience and education in a related field; an advanced degree may be considered in lieu of professional experience

• 2 years of related experience (Customer Success, Customer Service, Account Management or Sales)

Preferred Qualifications

• Experience supporting a SaaS application preferred

• Deep commitment to customer success - not just satisfaction

• Ability to understand complex problems and explain the source of those problems simply

• Strong communication and presentation skills with a high level of comfort in delivering consultative recommendations

• Self-starter with strong time management and prioritization skills

Travel Requirements & Working Conditions

• Willingness to travel up to 10% for team and corporate meetings, fostering relationships and representing company interests

• Reliable internet access for any period of time working remotely, as we embrace flexible work arrangements

Why Join Workiva

Workiva is the platform designed to bring confidence, control, and a competitive edge to the world’s most complex organizations. Our AI-powered platform unifies finance, risk, and sustainability on a single, secure foundation-ensuring data is trusted, traceable, and ready to act on. With an unbroken path from source to output, leaders gain confidence in their numbers, visibility into current and emerging risks, and the ability to move with speed and precision in a constantly changing world.
At Workiva , you’ll bring technology to market that executives, boards, and regulators depend on. The work you do here helps organizations navigate uncertainty, maintain trust, and make decisions that stand up to scrutiny. If you’re energized by meaningful challenges, inspired by collaborative teams, and motivated to help organizations turn uncertainty into advantage, we’d love to meet you.

We value diversity of backgrounds, beliefs, and interests, and we recognize diversity as an important source of intellectual thought, varied perspective, and innovation. Employment decisions are made without regard to age, gender identity, race, religion, disability status, sexual orientation, or any other protected characteristic.
